title: Iman Gadzhi on beginner-safe businesses, intentional personal brands, and why content rewards beat ads
summary: Iman Gadzhi explains why beginners should pick digital products or services where failure is cheap, how to build a personal brand around a specific business goal, and why intensity must give way to patience and rigid routines give way to new interests. He also shares his case for WAP's content rewards as an advertising channel.

principles.text: Beginners should pick businesses where failing costs little: digital products or services, not inventory or ad-heavy models.
principles.quote: I like businesses where you can fail for 6 months, 12 months. And by the way, I don't view anything as a failure. I view it as you're getting closer and closer

principles.text: Start with simple services or cheap products to get a foot in the door; don't copy the end-stage moves of someone far ahead.
principles.quote: So, I started off by doing simple services for local businesses. So, yeah. Is are these opportunities going to make you a multimillionaire? No. But it's it's your foot through the door.

principles.text: Be intentional with a personal brand: define the business benefit you want, and don't equate views with success.
principles.quote: number one mistake is not being intentional

principles.text: Match content to the buyer: split into niche channels so advice for a specific audience reaches that audience and funnels to the right back-end offer.
principles.quote: the more niche the advice the more niche the market.

principles.text: Content rewards (paying clippers and creators) can deliver reach at a fraction of Facebook ad CPMs while paying your fans instead of the platforms.
principles.quote: you're accomplishing advertising at like a, you know, 10% or 5% the CPM of what it would cost on Facebook.

principles.text: Hold urgency in the short term and patience in the long term; intensity gets you off the ground, but plateaus break when you loosen the routine and add interests.
principles.quote: short term you have to have this feeling of urgency but then in the more medium term you have to have this understanding that like you are young.
